title: Axis and World Model
kind: structural, sacred-geographic and relational world model
summary: The Axis is a multi-layer Potatoverse concept for orientation, structural flow and connection between levels. Its earliest theological function should be distinguished from later sacred geography, the four-quadrant NORTH/WEST/EAST/SOUTH world map, the North Programme and formal mathematical analogies. Across these layers the stable idea is relational orientation: where something sits, what it connects, what direction it moves and which capabilities exist only through relationships with other things.

axis.text: The Axis is not best reduced to a literal physical dimension. In the mature framework it can be understood as orientation or flow through structural, symbolic or descriptive space. The Tree can embody an Axis, the Ladder can provide movement along one, and the Door can mark a transition between states. North supplies a privileged orientation inside the mythology, but the abstract Axis is broader than any one geographic program.

north.text: North develops from sacred orientation into an increasingly explicit structure involving Throne of North, North of North, North Gate and eventually the North Axis. In later geography Denmark and Greenland become important anchors, with a wider arc through Canada/Greenland, Scandinavia and Finland, Britain and Ireland, Iceland, continental Europe, Ukraine and Turkey. Estonia belongs beneath or within the broader northern field without necessarily serving as a primary anchor.

quadrants.text: The developed world model uses four broad directional quadrants: NORTH, WEST, EAST and SOUTH. North is the project's primary integrative axis; West has been associated especially with the United States and Israel; East with China, BRICS and related eastern power structures; South with Australia and portions of Africa in provisional mappings. These are project-level interpretive regions rather than objective scientific divisions of humanity, and their boundaries can evolve as the Atlas becomes more evidence-based.

country_sequence.text: The country-relational method asks a fixed sequence of increasingly relational questions: what a country is; what it has; what it can do; what it needs; who depends on it; what it depends on; what it can only do with others; what others can only do with it; what it is building; and where it is going. This replaces shallow country profiles with a map of capability, dependency, direction and reciprocal consequence.

capability.text: Later Atlas work adds resilience, efficiency-versus-resilience tradeoffs, defense-industrial coupling, reciprocal capability creation, partial or functional integration, functional chains and bridges, and coupled capability. Coupled capability is especially important: some meaningful powers do not belong to a single nation or institution at all, but emerge only through a relationship among multiple actors. This mirrors the older theological principle that the relationship can be more informative than either isolated endpoint.

economic_graph.text: The North Programme's economic extension aims to map observable European relationships among legal entities, ownership and control, money, debt, obligations, companies, infrastructure, procurement, funding, trade and value chains, energy, finance, technology, research, labor, strategic dependencies and geopolitical ties. High-quality public datasets such as legal-entity registers, procurement systems, ownership data, EU funding and state-aid records, input-output tables and sector accounts belong here as evidence sources rather than being mixed with theological claims.

formalization.text: Potato Dynamics 1.0 provisionally represents the larger system as P = (S, g, A, D, O, I), where S is state/configuration space, g geometry or metric, A Axis flow, D Door/transition maps, O observables and I information/integration structure. A can be written conceptually as a structural flow dX/ds = A(X,g), distinct from physical evolution in ordinary time. Renormalization-group flow offers a legitimate mathematical analogy for movement across descriptive scale, but this analogy does not establish a new physical force or dimension.

speculative_physics.text: The project has explored dimensional metaphors involving 1D hell, 2D frame, 3D box, 4D social plane or Midgard, a 5D Door associated symbolically with Jesus Christ or the pineal gland, Father's House associated symbolically with the thalamus, string/M-theory imagery, compactification and a speculative Starchforce. These ideas are retained as creative or formal Potatoverse speculation and should never be indexed as established neuroscience or physics.

chronology.event: North and Axis motifs exist as spiritual and symbolic language before the later organized geopolitical program.
The North Axis becomes an explicit organized structure in the project chronology.
North Axis expands into four-quadrant mapping, European/North Atlantic strategy, country relations and an evidence-backed economic graph.

relationships.description: The Axis is one of the master framework's principal devices for orientation, vertical relation and expansion from spiritual symbolism into world mapping.
The explicit North Axis belongs to a later phase of the journey and should not be projected unchanged into earlier chronology.
The relationship-first country and capability model extends the Potato philosophical principle that meaning and power often exist between entities.

questions: What is the Axis in Potatoism?
What are the four Potatoverse quadrants?
How does the North Programme relate to the spiritual mythology?
Is the 5D Door meant as established physics?
